# Test the gecko import path forms: the "@" package prefix, relative imports
# that name a single file with an optional ".gk" extension, and the rules that
# pick between a directory and a file.

env GK111MODULE=off

# A gecko project (gecko.json, no go.mod) with a single-file package at the
# root and a main file next to it.
mkdir $WORK/proj
cp $WORK/gecko.json $WORK/proj/gecko.json
cp $WORK/utils.gk $WORK/proj/utils.gk
cp $WORK/logger.gk $WORK/proj/logger.gk
cp $WORK/main_at.gk $WORK/proj/main.gk

cd $WORK/proj

# "@utils" names the same package as "utils".
go run main.gk
stdout 'feat ok'

# The old spelling keeps working.
cp $WORK/main_plain.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout 'feat ok'

# The "@" prefix also reaches the standard library.
cp $WORK/main_std.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '42'

# A relative import naming a file, with and without the extension: both
# spell the same package, built from logger.gk alone.
cp $WORK/main_file_noext.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] hi'

cp $WORK/main_file_ext.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] hi'

# Without braces the file's own package clause supplies the name.
cp $WORK/main_file_qualified.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] qualified'

# The file is the whole package: a sibling file in the same directory is not
# part of it, even when it declares a different package.
cp $WORK/audit.gk audit.gk
cp $WORK/main_siblings.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
! stdout 'audit'
cp $WORK/main_sibling_leak.gk main.gk
! go run main.gk
stderr 'undefined: audit'
rm audit.gk

# A directory of that name wins over the file.
mkdir $WORK/proj/logger
cp $WORK/logger_dir.gk $WORK/proj/logger/lib.gk
cp $WORK/main_file_noext.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout 'DIR hi'

# An explicit "./logger.gk" still names the file.
cp $WORK/main_file_ext.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] hi'
rm -r $WORK/proj/logger

# A file package may import another file package.
cp $WORK/chain1.gk $WORK/proj/chain1.gk
cp $WORK/main_chain.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] chained'
rm $WORK/proj/chain1.gk

# A relative import also works from a library package of the project, not
# only from package main.
mkdir $WORK/proj/app
cp $WORK/app.gk $WORK/proj/app/app.gk
cp $WORK/main_lib.gk main.gk
go run main.gk
stdout '\[log\] de lib'

# An import cycle through file imports is still a cycle.
cp $WORK/cyc1.gk $WORK/proj/cyc1.gk
cp $WORK/cyc2.gk $WORK/proj/cyc2.gk
cp $WORK/main_cycle.gk main.gk
! go run main.gk
stderr 'import cycle not allowed'
stderr 'imports \./cyc1 from'
rm $WORK/proj/cyc1.gk $WORK/proj/cyc2.gk

# A missing file is reported with the file that was looked for.
cp $WORK/main_missing.gk main.gk
! go run main.gk
stderr 'cannot find file'

-- $WORK/gecko.json --
{
  "name": "script-import",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "dynamic"
}

-- $WORK/utils.gk --
package utils

export func feat(): string {
	return "feat ok"
}

-- $WORK/logger.gk --
package logger

export func rec(msg: string): string {
	return "[log] " + msg
}

-- $WORK/logger_dir.gk --
package logger

export func rec(msg: string): string {
	return "DIR " + msg
}

-- $WORK/audit.gk --
package audit

export func leaked(): string {
	return "audit"
}

-- $WORK/main_at.gk --
package main

import { feat } from "@utils"

func main() {
	println(feat())
}

-- $WORK/main_plain.gk --
package main

import { feat } from "utils"

func main() {
	println(feat())
}

-- $WORK/main_std.gk --
package main

import "@strconv"

func main() {
	println(strconv.Itoa(42))
}

-- $WORK/main_file_noext.gk --
package main

import { rec } from "./logger"

func main() {
	println(rec("hi"))
}

-- $WORK/main_file_ext.gk --
package main

import { rec } from "./logger.gk"

func main() {
	println(rec("hi"))
}

-- $WORK/main_file_qualified.gk --
package main

import "./logger.gk"

func main() {
	println(logger.rec("qualified"))
}

-- $WORK/main_siblings.gk --
package main

import { rec } from "./logger"

func main() {
	println(rec("siblings"))
}

-- $WORK/main_sibling_leak.gk --
package main

import "./logger"

func main() {
	println(audit.leaked())
}

-- $WORK/chain1.gk --
package chain1

import { rec } from "./logger.gk"

export func go2(): string {
	return rec("chained")
}

-- $WORK/main_chain.gk --
package main

import { go2 } from "./chain1"

func main() {
	println(go2())
}

-- $WORK/app.gk --
package app

import { rec } from "../logger.gk"

export func run(): string {
	return rec("de lib")
}

-- $WORK/main_lib.gk --
package main

import "app"

func main() {
	println(app.run())
}

-- $WORK/cyc1.gk --
package cyc1

import { two } from "./cyc2"

export func one(): string {
	return "one -> " + two()
}

-- $WORK/cyc2.gk --
package cyc2

import { one } from "./cyc1"

export func two(): string {
	return "two -> " + one()
}

-- $WORK/main_cycle.gk --
package main

import { one } from "./cyc1"

func main() {
	println(one())
}

-- $WORK/main_missing.gk --
package main

import { rec } from "./nothing"

func main() {
	println(rec("x"))
}
